title: Tracer Bug: Global Depth Counter Broken by Exceptions
description: Same tracer as Model 2 but with TODOs. _depth global not protected by try/finally. When ZeroDivisionError unwinds stack, _depth not decremented. Second attempt has wrong indentation (extra 2 spaces). TODO 1: wrap in try/finally to restore _depth. TODO 2: print numeric depth alongside indentation. Test: boom = 1 + (3/0), run twice. Attempt 1 correct; attempt 2 indented wrong (depth leaked).

steps.description: AST nodes: Num, Var, BinOp. Same as before.
evaluate_traced: manages _depth. indent = '  ' * _depth. Increments _depth, calls _eval_inner, decrements _depth, returns result. NO try/finally - if exception raised, _depth -= 1 skipped.
TODO 1: wrap in try/finally so _depth restored even when child raises. Run division-by-zero tree twice, confirm second trace indented correctly.
_eval_inner: TODO 2: print numeric depth. Num prints value. Var prints lookup. BinOp prints 'evaluating children...', recurses left/right, computes via ops dict, prints result.
Test: boom = 1 + (3/0). Loop runs twice. Attempt 1: evaluates, ZeroDivisionError caught. _depth left at wrong value. Attempt 2: indentation starts at wrong depth (extra 2 spaces).

steps.question: Why does the second attempt have incorrect indentation (extra spaces)?
steps.answer: First attempt: ZeroDivisionError raised in _eval_inner during '/' evaluation. Exception propagates out of evaluate_traced before _depth -= 1 runs. _depth remains incremented. Second attempt starts with _depth=1 instead of 0, so all indentation is off by 2 spaces.

steps.description: Output: Attempt 1 correct indentation. Attempt 2: all lines indented 2 extra spaces (e.g., '    BinOp...' instead of '  BinOp...'). ZeroDivisionError caught both times.
